issues.description: StockIngredient constructor signature mismatch: The problem statement (UML) declares a constructor StockIngredient(String, int, int), and the solution implementation provides a three-argument constructor public StockIngredient(String name, int price, int quantity). The template implementation only provides a four-argument constructor public StockIngredient(String name, int price, int quantity, boolean strictValidation). This prevents students from instantiating StockIngredient with the three-argument form shown in the problem examples and the reference solution and will cause compilation errors when following the exercise instructions.
issues.suggestedFix: Add the expected three-argument constructor to the template: public StockIngredient(String name, int price, int quantity). Implement it either by overloading (delegating to the existing four-argument constructor, e.g., this(name, price, quantity, true)) or by copying the validation/assignment logic from the solution's three-arg constructor. Alternatively, replace the current four-argument constructor with the three-argument version. This will align the template with the problem statement and the reference solution and allow students to instantiate StockIngredient as shown in examples.

issues.description: Constructor signature mismatch for StockIngredient: The problem statement's UML declares a constructor StockIngredient(String, int, int). The solution repository implements a public StockIngredient(String, int, int) constructor (solution/src/de/tum/cit/ase/StockIngredient.java). The template repository only provides a constructor StockIngredient(String, int, int, boolean) (template/src/de/tum/cit/ase/StockIngredient.java) and no three-argument overload. The template's Main (template/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Main.java) and the exercise text expect three-argument instantiations (e.g., new StockIngredient("Bacon", 10, 50)). This inconsistency will cause compilation errors and prevents students from mapping the UML/problem requirements to the provided template code.
issues.suggestedFix: Add a three-argument constructor public StockIngredient(String name, int price, int quantity) to the template StockIngredient class (either by overloading and delegating to the existing four-argument constructor or by providing an implementation equivalent to the solution). This will align the template API with the UML, the problem examples, and the reference solution and avoid compilation errors for three-argument instantiations.
